feature: Every value in the panel has a key diamond
summary: Pick a layer in a recording and the Animating section lists every value that can change over time, each with a diamond. Click one to start keying it at the playhead. From then on, changing that value at another moment, in the panel or by dragging on the canvas, adds a key.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a screen recording and type a title on it with the text tool.

try.do: With the title picked, scroll the panel to Animating and look at the dim diamonds beside Position, Scale, Rotation, Opacity, Color, Blur, Shadow size and Text size.
Click the diamond beside Scale. It fills: a key at the playhead.
Move the playhead two seconds later, type 160 into Scale and press Return. That is a second key.
Step back a second. The diamond is hollow, Scale reads part way, and the title on the canvas is part grown.
Click the ‹ and › arrows beside the diamond to jump between the two keys. Press Command Z to take the second key back.
Click the diamond beside Position, step back a second and drag the title on the canvas. The drag is a Position key; the title is still where it was a second later.
Click the lit Scale diamond. It asks before removing the keys, and the title keeps the size it has at the playhead.
Right-click any row for Add Key Here, Remove Key Here and Stop Animating.

evaluate: The diamond works as Premiere's stopwatch: click a lit one to stop animating, after a question. The mock instead has a filled diamond remove only the key under the playhead (that is on the row's right-click here). Keep the stopwatch?
Does listing every value, keyed or not, answer 'how do I animate this?' without making the section feel long?
Is a drag on the canvas turning into a key what you expect once Position is keyed, or should it ask the first time?
Are the three diamond states (dim, violet outline, violet fill) easy to tell apart at a glance?
rough: The old Motion section still shows a keyed value again as From, To, Start and Over rows, so the panel says one thing twice. It stays until a curve can be chosen on a key; folded into the lanes task.
The mock lists only what is animating, with an Animate a property button, and its own caption says every value should be listed. The app lists every value, as the task asks.
The mock has no key arrows; the task asked for them, so each keyed row has ‹ ◆ ›. Value boxes are narrow 52pt fields where the mock draws wide dark boxes; folded into the video properties look task.
Crop and glow cannot be keyed yet: crop needs a rectangle value. Left on the parent keyframe task.
The mock's Graph link and its Easing menu on the timeline bar are not here. A new key eases in and out, and the curve can still be changed in the Motion section.
